summary: Epochal pin drift after hotfix commit causes split-cohort model routing
description: Issue summary: After a hotfix commit was deployed to edge-proxy and serving-runtime, a subset of NimbusHealth tenant sessions began receiving responses from an older model variant despite tenant-level version pin. Impact: intermittent mixed-model responses and occasional semantic regressions in production traffic for a high-volume customer on Dedicated capacity. Scope: ~2% of requests for the tenant across two API routes were routed to legacy variant; visible for ~30 minutes during a regional rebalancing window.
impact: Customer-reported model inconsistencies (different generations for same session), increased error rate for downstream validation checks, and 3 customer-facing support cases opened. Business impact: potential quality regression for patient-facing summaries; customer flagged as escalated.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer has tenant-level pin to redwood/gpt-infer-v1.2.
2) Deploy hotfix that increments edge-proxy epoch used for cohort merges (edge hotfix applied at 08:22 UTC).
3) Trigger tenant traffic (steady load).
4) Observe that ~2% of requests return tokens with generation signatures matching older variant.
Note: issue reproduced in prod only when regional rebalancer moved a small number of routing shards at 08:46 UTC.
logs:
Edge trace snippets: span=edg-router-9345 trace_id=7f2a1c start=2026-03-10T08:46:03Z routing_decision=COHORT_MERGE epoch_old=89 epoch_new=90 pin_token=tn-9843 map_hash=0x4f3b
Serving runtime logs: warn: pin_coherence: token epoch mismatch for session tn-9843 expected=90 observed=89
Healthcheck events: probe=region-rebalancer shard_move=shard-137 => 24s delay
Request IDs: r-20260310-8f7a, r-20260310-8f7b, r-20260310-8f7c (samples attached in ticket).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: epoch increment during hotfix created a transient window where edge used new epoch while routing-coordinator still had cached cohort maps on old epoch. Evidence: routing_coordinator metrics show a 22s TTL eviction spike at 08:46:03Z; edge proxy shows commit timestamp 08:22 but persisted epoch header 90. Correlation with rebalancer: rebalancer log shows simultaneous shard moves which triggered local cache rebuilds and a race between pin reconciliation and cohort-merge reconciliation. Verified that fallback-routing was exercised because several backends returned 503 for the new variant; fallback routed to older variant that was still considered compatible.
root_cause: Race between edge hotfix rollout (epoch bump) and routing-coordinator cache invalidation during a shard rebalancing window. The epoch token in the pin header did not reconcile atomically across all routing layers; some routers accepted older epoch pin mapping and routed to legacy instances. Additionally, fallback policy allowed migration to legacy variant when a subset of nodes reported degraded health during the rollout.
workaround: 1) Temporary pin refresh: instruct customer to issue a pin-refresh API call which forces token re-issuance tied to epoch 90. 2) Increase routing-coordinator cache TTL to avoid immediate evictions during coordinated rollouts. Workaround applied at 09:05 UTC; customer reported reduction in mixed responses within 3 minutes.
resolution_plan: Short term: backport a coordination barrier so that serving-runtime and edge-proxy epoch bumps use an orchestrated commit fence during region rebalances (PR created: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/6123). Medium term: introduce pin-epoch handshake and optimistic validation on edge to detect mismatched epoch early and queue requests for atomic reconciliation. Ops action: a runbook update to pause shard rebalancer during hotfix epoch bumps for Dedicated tenants for next 30 days.
postmortem_followup: Action items: (1) add an e2e test that simulates epoch bump + shard move, (2) update canary rollout playbook to include atomic pin handshake, (3) increase observability: add metric 'pin_epoch_mismatch_rate' and dashboard, (4) schedule a customer check-in with NimbusHealth for 2026-03-13 16:00 UTC.
